analyst_view.overall: NEC (12th, 7 points) and Rennes (17th, 6 points) are both in the play-off places, and a win would push either toward the top eight. NEC beat Omonia 3-1 last time in Europe but lost 4-1 at home to PSV on Saturday and have leaked goals all season; Bram Nuytinck (ankle) is out and Perr Schuurs is out or doubtful (Schuurs counted, Nuytinck not), with Emre Mor also missing (counted). Rennes, under Franck Haise, have drawn three of four in this phase; Ouest-France reports they travel without both Mahdi Camara and Valentin Rongier, with a first call-up for youngster Ruben Lomet, Frankowski is out (counted), and one team-news page lists top scorer Esteban Lepaul (8 goals) as out with a sprained ankle, which I could not confirm elsewhere. Both sides play again in the league three days later, so some rotation is likely; Serbian referee Nenad Minakovic (about 3.9 cards a game) is already counted. The UEFA match page confirms Nenad Minakovic in charge and gives no fresh team news, so the view stands with Lepaul's status still unconfirmed.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.4 goals and already take about 9% off NEC for Schuurs and some off Rennes for Rongier and Frankowski. NEC without Nuytinck and Rennes without Camara (neither counted) point to a more open game, but one report has Lepaul, Rennes's main scorer, out with an ankle sprain, which would pull the other way; with that unconfirmed, the two roughly cancel and I drop yesterday's small lean higher and stay at 3.4.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.5 corners, already adjusted for NEC winning more corners lately (38 in six) and Rennes fewer. The absences are in NEC's defence and Rennes's central midfield and possibly up front, none of which changes how either side gets the ball wide, so I stay at 9.5.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.0 cards, with referee Nenad Minakovic slightly below average (3.9 a game) and Rennes's calm recent card count already in. There is no history between the sides and a younger, rotated Rennes midfield is not a clear sign of more fouls, so I stay at 4.0.

shots.text: The numbers say 29.2 shots, already raised for NEC's busy recent shooting (105 in six). Gaps in both teams could open the game, but likely rotation before the weekend and a possible Rennes attack without Lepaul pull the other way, so I stay at 29.2.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.4 shots on target, already up a little for NEC's sharp recent finishing (40 on target in six). NEC's weakened back line should give Rennes chances, but if Lepaul is missing Rennes lose their best finisher, so I drop yesterday's small lean and stay at 10.4.
